subject: anatomy
title: Carpal Tunnel Mechanics and Guyon Canal Anatomy

steps.tx: The anterior carpal arch is converted into a fibro-osseous conduit designated the **carpal tunnel** by the thick, inelastic flexor retinaculum (transverse carpal ligament). The flexor retinaculum attaches medially to the pisiform and hook of the hamate, and laterally to the tubercle of the scaphoid and crest of the trapezium.
steps.say: The carpal bones form a concave arch converted into the carpal tunnel by the dense transverse flexor retinaculum. The retinaculum bridges from the pisiform and hook of the hamate medially to the scaphoid and trapezium laterally.

vis.alt: Carpal bones, carpal tunnel arch, and wrist osseous boundaries
vis.caption: Carpal bones forming the floor and walls of the carpal tunnel. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The carpal tunnel transmits ten structures: four tendons of flexor digitorum superficialis, four tendons of flexor digitorum profundus, one tendon of flexor pollicis longus, and a single peripheral nerve, the **median nerve**. The tendon of flexor carpi radialis occupies a separate dedicated osseofibrous compartment within the lateral attachment.
steps.say: The carpal tunnel carries ten structures: four tendons of flexor digitorum superficialis, four of flexor digitorum profundus, the flexor pollicis longus tendon, and the median nerve. Flexor carpi radialis runs in a separate groove on the trapezium.

steps.tx: Compression of the median nerve within this rigid osteofibrous space produces **carpal tunnel syndrome**, the most common entrapment neuropathy. Patients experience nocturnal paresthesias, numbness, and burning pain across the radial three and a half digits, with weakness and atrophy of the thenar muscles (abductor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis, flexor pollicis brevis).
steps.say: Compression of the median nerve inside this rigid space produces carpal tunnel syndrome. Patients suffer nocturnal numbness and burning across the thumb, index, and middle fingers, progressing to thenar muscle wasting.

nodes.label: Median Nerve Capillary Ischemia and Edema

steps.tx: Crucially, sensation over the central palm is completely spared in carpal tunnel syndrome because the **palmar cutaneous branch of median nerve** arises five centimeters proximal to the flexor retinaculum and passes superficial to the transverse carpal ligament into the palm, avoiding entrapment within the tunnel.
steps.say: Importantly, sensation over the palm is spared in carpal tunnel syndrome because the palmar cutaneous branch arises five centimeters above the wrist and travels superficial to the retinaculum, bypassing the tunnel entirely.

steps.tx: Clinical provocation tests confirm median nerve entrapment: **Phalen test** reproduces paresthesias within sixty seconds of unforced maximal wrist flexion, while Tinel sign elicits electrical tingling upon tapping over the volar carpal retinaculum. Severe cases show ape hand deformity with flat thenar eminence and loss of thumb opposition.
steps.say: Provocation maneuvers confirm carpal tunnel syndrome: Phalen test reproduces numbness within sixty seconds of sustained wrist flexion, while Tinel sign triggers tingling upon tapping the retinaculum. Severe cases show an ape-like flat thenar pad.

rows: Direct thumb pressure over carpal tunnel

steps.tx: On the medial volar aspect of the wrist lies the **Guyon canal** (ulnar tunnel), bounded medially by the pisiform, laterally by the hook of the hamate, roofed by the volar carpal ligament and palmaris brevis, and floored by the flexor retinaculum. It transmits the ulnar artery and ulnar nerve into the hand.
steps.say: On the medial side of the wrist lies the Guyon canal, bounded by the pisiform and hook of hamate, roofed by the volar carpal ligament. It transmits the ulnar artery and ulnar nerve into the hand superficial to the carpal tunnel.

vis.alt: Ulnar artery and nerve entering palm via Guyon canal and superficial arch
vis.caption: Ulnar neurovascular transit through the Guyon canal into the palm. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Compression of the ulnar nerve within Guyon canal produces **ulnar tunnel syndrome**, frequently seen in long-distance cyclists who exert prolonged hypothenar handlebar pressure (handlebar palsy). Within the canal, the ulnar nerve divides into a superficial sensory branch supplying the medial one and a half digits, and a deep motor branch.
steps.say: Ulnar nerve compression in Guyon canal produces ulnar tunnel syndrome, common in cyclists from prolonged handlebar pressure. In the canal, the nerve splits into a superficial sensory branch to the little finger and a deep motor branch.

right.title: Guyon Canal Syndrome
points: Preserves sensation over dorsal ulnar hand

steps.tx: Fractures of the **hook of the hamate** from golf club or baseball bat strikes selectively injure the deep motor branch of the ulnar nerve as it curves around the bone hook. This produces isolated motor paralysis of all interossei, the hypothenar muscles, and adductor pollicis without any sensory loss, creating a pure motor claw hand.
steps.say: Fractures of the hook of the hamate from golf clubs can injure the deep motor branch of the ulnar nerve. This produces isolated motor weakness of all interossei and hypothenar muscles without sensory loss.
